title: Adaptive segment prioritizer for runtime micro-batching to reduce padding and improve kernel selection
creator: Jonah Kepler
description:
Background: Our current micro-batching pipeline groups requests primarily by sequence-length buckets and arrival time. This reduces padding overall but often mixes requests whose attention patterns (context reuse, prefill vs decode state, and KV-cache lifetimes) cause suboptimal kernel selection and extra memory traffic during prefill. On busy tails we also observe latency spikes when long prefills force the batch into a slow kernel and inflate padding for shorter decodes.

Goals: 1) Reduce effective padding across mixed prefill+decode workloads by prioritizing segment-level packing rather than just per-request length bucketing. 2) Improve kernel selection accuracy by exposing per-segment runtime hints so the scheduler can pick kernels (dense vs fused attention, sparse variants) that match segment characteristics. 3) Maintain or improve 95th/99th percentile latency SLO while preserving throughput and lowering token cost.

Proposal (high-level): Introduce an "Adaptive Segment Prioritizer" (ASP) in the prefill/dispatcher layer that operates on a lightweight segmentation of incoming requests. A segment is a contiguous region of a request that will share the same KV-cache affinity and attention window (e.g., user message block vs system prompt vs trailing decode). The ASP will:
- Inspect incoming envelopes and prefill/decode intents to emit per-segment metadata: seq_len, is_prefill, kv_lifetime_hint, attention_window_hint, entropy_estimate.
- Run a short-lived prioritization heuristic that groups segments into micro-batches to minimize padding while maximizing kernel affinity. Heuristics include: length-closeness threshold, prefilling-first weighting, and kernel-affinity score.
- Emit kernel hints to the runtime allocator so the kernel selector can test the top-2 kernels for compatibility (e.g., fused attention for short dense segments, memory-slight kernels for long sparse segments).
- Schedule prefill segments earlier when they enable KV caching opportunities for following decodes from the same session, but avoid holding back decode-latency-critical segments behind long prefills by splitting slow-prefill segments across two micro-batches if necessary.

Attention optimizations: For segments with small attention windows or repeated system prompt fragments we will attempt attention-slicing: compute attention for shared prefix once and reference it across segments in the same micro-batch, reducing duplicate matmul work. For long-context segments where sparse attention kernels are a win, ASP will bias packing to create a contiguous group large enough to amortize the sparse kernel startup cost.

Prefill/Decode scheduling: The dispatcher will maintain two small queues (prefill-priority and decode-fastpath). The ASP assigns segments to queues with a tunable score; the scheduler will interleave micro-batches from both queues using a ratio that targets our latency SLOs while letting prefills proceed to enable cache reuse.

Implementation notes:
- Minimal changes to runtime: add a per-microbatch "kernel_hint" field and a tiny API for runtime to return warm-up cost metrics.
- Add a new stat stream from dispatcher: segment_packed_ratio, avg_padding_tokens_per_batch, kernel_hint_accuracy, kv_reuse_rate.
- Conservative rollout: feature flag behind runtime-1.20, with canary gating per-region and per-customer-tier.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reduction in avg padding tokens per useful token by >= 12% on mixed prefill/decode workloads (internal benchmark suite).
- No degradation to P95 token latency > 5% in canary region.
- Kernel hint accuracy (selected kernel matches top measured kernel) >= 80% after 2k batches.
- End-to-end e2e tests and integration tests for KV reuse cases (session reuse, multi-message flows).

Rollout plan:
1) Unit implementation in dispatcher (feature-flagged) + telemetry (non-blocking) — run for 2 days in staging.
2) Small canary with low-traffic hostnames in a single region; examine kernel_hint_accuracy and avg_padding metrics (48h).
3) Broader canary across traffic classes with gradual ramp and auto rollback if P95 exceeds threshold.
4) Full rollout to runtime-1.20 if canary pass criteria.

Metrics to track:
- avg_padding_tokens_per_batch (per-model)
- token_cost_per_second and token_cost_per_request
- kv_reuse_rate (sessions benefiting from prefill re-use)
- kernel_hint_accuracy
- P50/P95/P99 latency per request type (prefill vs decode)
- throughput (tokens/sec)

Risks and mitigation:
- Mispacking could harm latency for latency-sensitive decodes: mitigate with conservative scoring and a fastpath queue that always prioritizes short decode segments.
- Kernel hint misprediction might cause extra kernel switches and overhead: we will probe only the top-2 candidates and fall back automatically; metricize warm-up cost.
- Complexity increases in dispatcher: keep heuristics compact and tunable config with safe defaults.

Notes about experiments to run (initial):
- Synthetic mixed traffic run (1M requests) with 70/30 decode/prefill ratio, compare baseline vs ASP enabled.
- Real-customer replay for two customers with heavy multi-message sessions (internal privacy-preserving replay).
- Microbench per-kernel to measure break-even length for sparse vs dense attention kernels.

Deliverables:
- Dispatcher changes (feature-flagged), runtime small API extension for kernel_hint and warmup metrics, telemetry dashboard, and a Confluence design doc describing heuristics and tuning knobs.
